speaker: Doctor
text: I will begin by asking: Have you noticed any specific triggers for your neck and arm pain, such as certain positions or activities? Additionally, have you experienced any recent trauma to the neck or upper spine?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy with Radiculopathy.

Given your 58 years of age, the one-year history of burning neck and arm pain, the recent progression of hand weakness, and your vascular risk factors, the most likely cause is cervical spinal stenosis compressing the spinal cord and nerve roots. To confirm this, I will request imaging of your cervical spine. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Cervical_Spine.
